response:
Here is a paragraph using words that contain only three types of vowels:

"Ape, axe, and ace men ate axe-ripe aubergines. Ape men ate axe-ripe aubergines and axe-ripe apricots. Ape men ate axe-ripe aubergines and axe-ripe apricots, and axe-ripe apples. Ape men ate axe-ripe aubergines and axe-ripe apricots, and axe-ripe apples, and axe-ripe aubergines."

And here is the timeline of mankind:

The first lone caveman, Gronk, emerged from the primordial ooze 2.5 million years ago. He stumbled upon a ripe aubergine and devoured it, marking the beginning of the human species. As the ages passed, humans evolved and spread across the globe, developing complex societies and harnessing the power of fire.

Around 10,000 BCE, humans began to domesticate animals, leading to the rise of agriculture and the development of cities. The pyramids of Giza were built, and the ancient civilizations of Egypt, Mesopotamia, and Greece flourished.

As the centuries passed, humans continued to innovate and explore, leading to the Age of Exploration and the discovery of the New World. The Industrial Revolution transformed the world, and humans began to colonize the moon and establish space stations.

In the 21st century, humans made contact with alien life forms and formed the United Earth Government. The world was united under a single banner, and humans began to explore the cosmos in earnest.

And then, without warning, every single human being who had ever come into existence was suddenly transported to a replica of Earth, infinite in size and scope. The last lone astronaut, a being known only as "Echo," floated in the void, surrounded by the echoes of humanity's past.

As the infinite replica of Earth unfolded before them, humans began to rebuild and restart. They formed new societies, harnessed new technologies, and explored the infinite possibilities of their new home.

Gronk, the first caveman, looked out upon the infinite landscape and smiled, knowing that his legacy lived on. The aubergines were ripe, the apricots were ripe, and the apples were ripe. The cycle of life had begun anew, and humanity was ready to take its place among the stars.
